4. The defendants 1 to 3 by a joint written statement denied the allegations of the plaintiff and asserted that the Heba-bil-ewaj deed got by defendants 1 and 2 was a genuine document and defendants 1 and 2 got full title on the basis of that deed in respect of the 14th schedule of the suit land wherein the plaintiff did not inherit any share. The defendants further pleaded that the plaintiff was aware of the Heba-bil-ewaj deed from the very date of its execution and consequently the present suit which was filed on 22-10-76 was hopelessly barred by limitation. 

 5. The learned Subordinate Judge found all the issues in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner and decreed the suit. On appeal the learned Additional District Judge held that the suit was barred by limitation as the plaintiff-petitioner had knowledge of the Heba-bil-ewaj deed on the very date of its execution and the suit was filed long after 3 years front the date of knowledge. 

 6. Mr. A.T.M. Kamrul Islam, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner submits that the learned Additional District Judge wrongly held that the limitation of the suit will be governed by Article 91 or the Limitation Act though the present suit not being a suit to cancel or set aside the Heba-bil-ewaj deed the said Article was not applicable at all and so the question of knowledge of the Heba-bil-ewaj deed was immaterial. He submitted that Article 93 of the limitation Act would be applicable in this case because the defendants having attempted to enforce the Heba-bil-ewaj deed against the plaintiff as the suit was to be filed within 3 years from the date of such attempt. Mr. Kamrul Islam submitted that in this suit the plaintiff pleaded that in the later part of Sraban 1383 B.S. i.e. in the first part of August, 1976 it was for the first time disclosed that the defendants 1 and 2 had obtained Heba-bil-ewaj deed for the 14th schedule land and it was only at that time that the defendants 1 to 3 attempted to enforce the allegedly forged deed and this was well borne out by the evidence. So the present suit which was filed on 22-10-76 that is within 2 months of the date suit was within time according to Article 93 of the Limitation Act. Thus Mr. Kamrul Islam pleaded that the learned Subordinate judge had rightly applied Article 93 of the Limitation Act. 

 7. On the other hand Mr. Mosih-ul Islam, the learned Advocate for the defendant-opposite parties submitted that in this suit there was absolutely no pleading to the effect that the defendant ever attempted to enforce the deed of Heba-bil-ewaj against the plaintiff and there was also no evidence on that score. So the learned Additional District Judge rightly held that Article 93 of the limitation Act was not applicable and also that he rightly found that the suit was barred by limitation as it was filed long over 3 years after the knowledge of the Heba-bil-ewaj deed in view of the Article 91 of the Limitation Act. 

 8. So the moot question to be decided is whether the present suit was barred by limitation or not and which Article of the limitation act will apply. 

 10. In his deposition the said plaintiff simply stated that For partition of their share Sarabanu and Abejan filed partition suit no.18 of 1971 and in that suit Shamser and Monser filed written statement in which it was first disclosed that plaintiff's father had executed a deed of Heba-bil-ewaj in favour of defendants 1 and 2 and the disclosure was made in Sraban 1383 and thereafter the plaintiff obtained certified copy of the deed. Throuldi out his deposition he did not say that the defendants ever made any attempt to enforce the Heba-bil-ewaj deed against the plaintiff. All that he said was that on the disclosure of the deed the defendants 1 to 3 have been claiming title without specifying when the said claim was made. Thus upon the pleading and evidence it cannot be said at all that the defendants having attempted to enforce the Heba-bil-ewaj deed that was the cause of action for the suit. On the contrary according to the pleading and evidence of the plaintiff because it was disclosed in the written statement of partition suit no.I8 of 1971 that the Heba-bil-ewaj deed was obtained by defendants 1 and 2 from the plaintiff's father and as that document was a forged one and cast cloud on the plaintiff's title in respect of the 14th schedule land so he brought the present suit. Thus upon the pleading and evidence of the plaintiff it must be held that Article 93 had no application to the present suit. On the other hand since it was a suit simply for declaring the forgery of a document registered the period of limitation of this suit will be governed by Article 92 of the limitation Act which means that the suit will have to be brought within 3 years from the date when the issue or registration of the deed is known to the plaintiff. So the learned Additional District Judge appears to be right in so far lie found that the suit was required to be filed within 3 years from the plaintiff's knowledge of the Heba-bil-ewaj deed. 

 11. It is now to be seen whether the suit was brought within 3 years from the plaintiff's knowledge of the Heba-bil-ewaj deed. In this respect the learned Additional District Judge found that the plaintiff himself had clearly stated in his own evidence that it was in Baisakh/ Jaistha 1372 13.5. corresponding to 26-5-65 that the plaintiff was informed about the Heba-bil-ewaj deed by Shamser, Sabder and Monser and on the basis of that statement of the plaintiff himself the learned Additional District Judge found that the plaintiff having knowledge of the Heba-bil-ewaj deed from the very date of the document namely 26-5-65 and the present suit having been filed on 22-10-76 the suit was hopelessly barred by limitation. Besides that when the plaintiff got knowledge of the Heba-bil-ewaj deed being a pure question of facts the finding of the appellate court cannot be questioned by this Court. 

 12. In the result, it is found that the learned Additional District Judge rightly held that the plaintiff’s suit was barred by limitation having been filed long beyond 3 years from the date of the knowledge of the Heba-bil-ewaj deed. 

 13. Besides the point of limitation there was no dispute raised in this court regarding the findings of the courts below on all the other issues in the suit. Thus it is found that the judgment and decree passed by the learned Additional District Judge suffer from no illegality in regard to exercise or non-exercise of proper jurisdiction and as such there is no scope to interfere with the same.
